title: Editing like a pro
explanation: You're the treasurer of a campus club, and the budget needs fixing before the meeting: a typo, an item to remove, a new item to add, and a new column. This lesson shows how to edit a sheet quickly and safely.

tasks.prompt: A3 has a typo: "speeker". Click A3, press the keys shown to edit the cell, and fix it to Guest speaker.
tasks.teach: Typing into a cell replaces everything. To change just **part** of a cell, press **F2** on Windows (**Ctrl+U** on Mac). Your cursor appears inside the cell, so you can use the arrow keys and fix one letter.
hints: Click A3, press the edit keys, move to the typo, and fix it. Then press Enter.

tasks.prompt: Practise undo: type 999 into B2 by mistake and press Enter. Then undo it, so Pizza night is back to 180.
tasks.teach: **Undo** (Ctrl+Z, or ⌘+Z on Mac) takes back your last change. Press it again to go back further. It's the most useful shortcut there is.
hints: Type 999 in B2, press Enter, then press the undo keys.
Hold Ctrl (⌘ on Mac) and press Z.
tasks.answer: Type 999 in B2, then press Ctrl+Z (⌘+Z on Mac)

tasks.prompt: The club doesn't need the old banner. Delete row 5: right-click the row number 5 on the left, and choose Delete.
tasks.teach: To remove a whole row, right-click its **number** on the left edge and choose **Delete**. The rows below move up to fill the gap, and formulas update to match.
hints: Right-click the grey 5 at the far left, not a cell.
After deleting, T-shirts should move up into row 5.

tasks.prompt: Add a row for snacks above Total: right-click the row number 6 (Total) and choose Insert.
tasks.teach: **Insert** adds an empty row above the one you right-clicked, and pushes everything below it down.
hints: Right-click the grey 6 at the far left, then choose the option to insert a row above.
Total should move down to row 7, leaving row 6 empty.

tasks.prompt: In the new row 6, type Snacks in A6, press Tab, type 240, then press Enter.
tasks.teach: **Enter** saves and moves **down**, but **Tab** saves and moves **right**. Use Tab to fill in a row across, without touching the mouse.
hints: Click A6, type Snacks, press Tab, type 240, press Enter.
tasks.answer: Snacks in A6, then Tab, then 240 in B6

tasks.prompt: Click B7 and look at the Total's formula. A row added at the very end of a range is often left out. Make sure the total includes Snacks: retype it as =SUM(B2:B6). It should come to 1250.
tasks.teach: When you add rows at the **edge** of a range, always check that your totals include them. It's one of the most common spreadsheet mistakes.
hints: The costs are now in B2 to B6.

tasks.prompt: Last one: add a column for who's in charge. Right-click the column letter B, choose Insert, then type Owner in the new B1.
tasks.teach: Columns work the same way: right-click the **letter** at the top and choose Insert to add one to the left. Notice the costs and the total move to column C, and the formula follows them.
hints: Right-click the grey B at the top, then insert a column to the left.
The new column B is empty. Type Owner in B1, and Cost moves to C.
tasks.answer: Insert a column at B, then type Owner in B1

recap: F2 (Ctrl+U on Mac) edits inside a cell, and Ctrl+Z or ⌘+Z undoes. Tab moves right and Enter moves down. Right-click a row number or column letter to insert or delete, and check your totals afterwards.
